parsed.rationale: Both `SoundCloudService.fetchMetadata` (SoundCloudService.swift:50) and `YouTubeMusicService.fetchMetadata` (YouTubeMusicService.swift:64) live in the same `MusicShareKit` package and exhibit a high structural similarity (Jaccard 0.808), indicating near-duplicate implementations of the same conceptual operation across two distinct music-service types. Introducing a `MusicMetadataFetchable` protocol with a `fetchMetadata` requirement in the `MusicShareKit` package would unify the contract, allow a default implementation to cover the shared logic, and leave only service-specific divergences in each conforming type. This is the most idiomatic Swift approach because the two types are parallel service abstractions rather than a class hierarchy, making a protocol-with-associated-type (or a plain protocol if `Metadata` is a concrete shared type) the natural abstraction boundary.
